Results.ReviewText: I bought the grill online from Home Depot. Assembly at home was fine and easy to follow. As the last step, following the instructions, I did the gas leak test with soapy water. The point of the hose where it exits the regulator had a leak (made big bubbles in the soap water). The instructions say if there’s a leak there to turn it all off and contact customer service. I have been trying to get in touch with someone from Weber customer service via phone and email/online contact form for over a month. I have received no response except the automated response email that confirms they received your message. I filled out the registration, made a warranty claim, have sent it in as a customer service question, etc., all with absolutely no response. I’m now buying a replacement hose myself from the Weber website in an attempt to have a useable grill. Very disappointed.
Results.Title: No customer service

Results.ReviewText:
When I received the grill, unfortunately one of the key parts was bent (and unusable), but Weber's customer service was really easy to work with and they sent me the replacement part pretty quickly. 

Once I received the part, I was surprised and how easy the grill was to assemble. I did it solo in under an hour (from start of step 1 to the final testing of it). Removing all the pieces from the box and dealing with the packaging probably took an additional 20-30 minutes. 

The grill itself has worked really well. The grates are wide enough that smaller things (like the inside rings of a sliced onion) don't easily fall through. The cooking surface is also shielded on three sides, so food does not roll off easily. So far (4 uses) the grill does not get up to super high heats with the lid closed, but does get up to 450-500 degrees if left closed. The grill has worked well with a 14"x11" plancha and gets/keeps the cast iron well heated. The side tables have been pretty sturdy so far, showing no signs of bending when I put meats and cutting boards on them. And the clip that holds the propane tank seems to be working really well--it's nice to see the tank getting lower and to have a consistent and quality seal between the tank and the tubing.

Overall, I'm really happy with the grill. I thought it was a touch pricey when I bought it, but there's value in what you're paying for. Would recommend this grill (or the two burner) to anyone who asks.
Results.Title: Good value, quality product

Photos.Caption: This grill actually makes your yard more beautiful! No more junky charcoals bags, starters stacks. This grill s much better looking than other gas grills that I checked out.

Results.ReviewText:
If you're ready for an upgrade from a charcoal grill, the Spirit II Series is for you! Although I loved for 20+ years, my reliable Weber kettle charcoal grill, I was ready to switch to the ease of gas. It is wonderful to go into the backyard and grill lunch or dinner at a moments notice, without having to fire up the coals in advance- if I even had coals on hand. And I can still get that charcoal smoky flavor by putting wood chips wrapped in foil on the grill. Now grilling is a breeze. I can even slow cook and roast  meats by placing them on cool side of my 3-burner grill. Grilling ribs over low heat for 2-1/2 hours used to be a hassle, now it's so easy. The meat falls off the bone it's so tender.
 
This grill is well designed and easy to use, with the 2 side shelves, hooks and bottom storage shelf. There is a warming rack. The cooking surface is nearly double what I had before. And to boot, this grill is really good looking. It completes our backyard. I LOVE my Spirit II!! Buy one, you will not be sorry.
Results.Title: Best cooking and good looking gas grill!
